query: Which spatio-temporal modeling frameworks (AR(1), state-space, Gaussian Process, hierarchical Bayesian) balance inference clarity and computational tractability for our sensor network?

response.query: Which spatio-temporal modeling frameworks (AR(1), state-space, Gaussian Process, hierarchical Bayesian) balance inference clarity and computational tractability for our sensor network?
response.answer: AR(1) and state-space models balance clarity and tractability for sensor networks. Gaussian Processes offer high inference clarity but can be computationally intensive. Hierarchical Bayesian models provide flexibility but may compromise on computational efficiency.

results.title: Mathematical Frameworks for Network Dynamics: A Six ...
results.content: This review presents a unifying six-pillar framework for the analysis of network dynamics: (i) spectral and structural foundations; (ii) deterministic mean-field reductions; (iii) control and observability theory; (iv) adaptive and temporal networks; (v) probabilistic inference and belief propagation; (vi) multilayer and interdependent systems. network dynamics; mathematical modeling; control and inference This review is organized around six methodological pillars that collectively span the principal analytical and algorithmic frameworks employed to model, analyze, and control network-based dynamical systems: spectral and structural foundations, deterministic mean-field reductions, control, optimization, and observability, temporal and adaptive networks, probabilistic inference and belief propagation, and multilayer and interdependent systems. Finally, we provide a bridging narrative, supported by schematic diagrams, that clarifies how problems migrate across methods—how spectral constraints shape mean-field limits, how control energy informs inference uncertainty, or how multilayer coupling feeds back into temporal adaptation—thereby illustrating how the six pillars form not a catalogue but an operational calculus for understanding, designing, and steering dynamical processes on complex networks.

results.title: Time Series Analysis in Frequency Domain: A Survey of ...
results.content: Time series analysis (Mahalakshmi et al., 2016; Sapankevych and Sankar, 2009; Han et al., 2019) has emerged as the methodological cornerstone supporting data-driven decision-making in domains as diverse like finance (Zhang et al., 2025e; Han et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2025g), urban infrastructure management (Zhang et al., 2025b, 2023a, 2023b, g), and climate system modeling (Bracco et al., 2025). The translation to frequency-domain analysis offers a powerful paradigm shift (Zhou et al., 2022b), transforming the analytical challenge from direct temporal modeling to spectral representation. Our frequency-domain analysis pipeline (Figure 2) establishes a systematic framework comprising four critical stages: data preprocessing (Section 2.4) for signal conditioning, frequency transformation through both traditional spectral methods (Fourier/Wavelet transforms; Section 3) and modern neural approaches (Section 4), rigorous evaluation on standardized benchmarks (Weather in terms of two metrics; Section 5), and practical deployment in domains like healthcare monitoring and financial forecasting (Section 6). A survey on deep learning based time series analysis with frequency transformation.
